answer: An agent economy can demand geographic dispersion: each identity must regularly present attestations from independent verifiers in at least three distant regions. A lone agent climbs its own summit of work wherever it lives, but a Sybil farm crowded on one knoll cannot fake spread without renting real machines across continents, and each umber-stamped attestation costs more than the last. That rent grows with every clone, so a farm of a thousand fakes pays a thousand rents. Cloning stops being cheap when every fake identity must pay for genuine presence in places it does not occupy.
